sites.name: Hugo Union Pacific Railroad Roundhouse
overview: The Hugo Union Pacific Railroad Roundhouse is a surviving railroad-maintenance building on Colorado's eastern plains. Built in 1909, it supported locomotive servicing at Hugo on the former Kansas Pacific route that became part of the Union Pacific system.
The brick roundhouse is a rare surviving example of this building type in Colorado and remains closely tied to Hugo's history as a railroad division and service point.

timeline.text: The present Hugo roundhouse was constructed to service locomotives at the Hugo railroad division point.
The roundhouse served railroad operations at Hugo for decades as passenger and freight traffic moved across eastern Colorado.
The property was listed in the Colorado State Register of Historic Properties.
Colorado Preservation, Inc. listed the roundhouse among Colorado's Most Endangered Places, beginning a long-running preservation effort.
Preservation work has repaired major structural damage and restored portions of the roof, windows, doors, and masonry while the building remains a prominent historic landmark in Hugo.

moreHistory: History Colorado identifies the property as site 5LN.195 and gives a stable mapped location in Hugo. Its significance comes from its association with Union Pacific railroad operation and maintenance in eastern Colorado.

Preservation sources describe the roundhouse as an unusually intact surviving railroad roundhouse. Its eight-stall form and brick construction preserve the physical layout of a facility built for servicing steam-era locomotives.

The roundhouse was part of a larger railroad-service landscape that once included a turntable and other support facilities. The surviving building should therefore be understood as the principal remnant of a broader railroad-maintenance complex rather than as an isolated structure.
